solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: No amateur cricketer, I! One getting runs as young professional?

parts.note: someone who is not an amateur is a pro, a professional
a bat is a batsman, a cricketer who wields the bat
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricketer insists they are no amateur, but one scoring runs as a young professional.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface keeps you in cricket, but the definition is a trainee on trial in any job, with a question mark because a probationer need not be young.
explanation.definitionFit: A probationer is a newcomer on trial in a job, a beginner professional still proving themselves.

clue.text: Paper makes point about cunning fellows

indicators.note: the abbreviation for point goes round the other pieces, so about signals one piece enclosing another

parts.note: arch means sly or knowing, so cunning
men are fellows

explanation.surface: A document claims to make a point about some crafty characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Parchment is prepared animal skin used for writing, an old kind of paper.

clue.text: Be on top of appalling evil or expire finally

indicators.note: something appalling is dreadful, so the letters of evil or are set in a dreadful new order
finally points to the closing letter of the word expire

explanation.surface: A ghoulish line about rising above dreadful evil or else dying at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appalling' rearranges EVILOR into OVERLI, and 'finally' takes E, the last letter of 'expire'.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlie something is to lie over it, resting on top of it.

clue.text: Bill, charming little son, keeps up to date

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
quaint means old-fashioned and charming
S is the short form, or little version, of son

explanation.surface: A bill arrives for a charming little boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquaint someone is to inform them, keeping them up to date with news.

clue.text: I love to absorb short publication: 'The Mature Insect'

indicators.note: the pair of letters takes in another piece, so absorb signals one piece going inside

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shown as the letter O
mag is the shortened form of magazine, a publication

explanation.surface: Someone declares their love of reading a short magazine piece called The Mature Insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final adult stage of an insect after metamorphosis.

clue.text: Chronicle English sailor managed to set up

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the whole string is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A tale of an English seaman who managed to get something established.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns ETARRAN round to give the answer, in a down clue read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To chronicle events is to record or tell them in order, a synonym for recounting them.

clue.text: Game lord has no right to make money

parts.note: RU stands for rugby union, a game

indicators.note: has no right means the letter for right is removed from the word for a lord

parts.note: a peer is a lord

explanation.surface: A nobleman with no rights plays a game to earn money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no right' takes R (right) out of PEER, leaving PEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency unit of India, Pakistan and other countries.

clue.text: Dispute about prosperous region being less moral?

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word for a dispute runs backwards

parts.note: a row is a dispute or quarrel
SE, the South East of England, is its wealthiest region

explanation.surface: An argument about a wealthy area turns on whether it has lower ethical standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispute' looks like the definition, but it supplies the reversed piece. The South East is England's wealthiest region, around London.
explanation.definitionFit: Worse is the comparative of bad, so someone worse behaved is less moral.

clue.text: Metallic material that could be seen in inro

parts.note: an inro is a Japanese box; its letters are the word iron worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A metal that might be spotted in a Japanese lacquered box.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: IRON wrought (worked) gives INRO, the last word of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrought iron is a tough, malleable form of the metal shaped by hammering.

clue.text: Animal with fleshy fruit seen in courtyard

indicators.note: one piece is seen inside the other, so these words signal putting one within another

parts.note: a quad is a quadrangle, a college courtyard
a drupe is a fleshy stone fruit like a plum

explanation.surface: Something with fleshy fruit spotted in a courtyard turns out to be an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadruped is any four-footed animal.

clue.text: Detest sin in awkward believer with different views

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy, so the letters of detest sin in are put together clumsily in another order

explanation.surface: Someone who hates sin is uncomfortable around believers who think differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissentient is someone who dissents, holding views different from the majority.

clue.text: Tragic woman and husband appearing in work by essayist

indicators.note: the abbreviation for husband appears inside the other pieces

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A tragic woman and her husband feature in an essayist's work.
explanation.walkthrough: ELIA is the pen name Charles Lamb used for his essays, a crossword standby.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophelia is the tragic heroine of Hamlet who drowns after going mad.

clue.text: Queen surrounded by old horses and asses

indicators.note: the Queen's letters are surrounded by the other pieces

parts.note: nags are horses
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen among old horses and donkeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Onagers are wild asses of Asia.

clue.text: Land held by single benefice?

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the run of words single benefice, so the answer is concealed there

explanation.surface: A question about the land belonging to one church living.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition-by-example hint in the question mark: the hidden word is itself land held by a benefice, so the clue reads as a whole as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Glebe is church land, an archaic word for soil or a field.

clue.text: Nobody should eat earthy matter — that's most important

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the word for nobody encloses the other piece

parts.note: none means nobody
umber is a brown earth used as pigment

explanation.surface: Nobody should eat dirt, and that is the top priority.
explanation.definitionFit: Number one, as a phrase, means the chief or foremost thing, the top priority.

clue.text: Oily stuff a female in need of education put into cocktail

parts.note: marg is short for margarine, an oily spread
Rita is the heroine of the play and film Educating Rita

explanation.surface: Margarine and an uneducated woman are put into a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is a Willy Russell play and film about a woman seeking an education.
explanation.definitionFit: A margarita is a tequila cocktail served with salt on the rim.

clue.text: Specially got up? Not I, not joining in

indicators.note: specially means arranged for a purpose, so the letters of got up not I are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether they are dressed up for the occasion replies that they are not.
explanation.definitionFit: Opting out means choosing not to take part, staying out of an activity.

clue.text: Aristotle worked out a betting system

indicators.note: worked out means solved or reshaped, so the philosopher's letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Aristotle devised a method for gambling.
explanation.walkthrough: A totaliser is the tote, which pools bets and shares the winnings among winners.
explanation.definitionFit: A totaliser is the pool-betting machine, the tote, that calculates payouts.

clue.text: Religious rite — the thing needed when there's disease around

indicators.note: the disease goes around the other piece

parts.note: the lurgy is jokey British slang for an unspecified illness
it means the thing in question

explanation.surface: Something is needed when a sickness is going round.
explanation.walkthrough: The lurgy, often 'the dreaded lurgy', is British slang for any infectious illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Liturgy is the prescribed form of public worship in a church.

clue.text: This person holds holy books before start of the anthem

indicators.note: before places the first part ahead of the next
the speaker holds the other piece inside

parts.note: this person is the speaker, me
OT is the Old Testament, a set of holy books

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A speaker holds scripture before the anthem begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' takes T from 'the', and 'anthem' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short choral composition, often sacred, much like an anthem.

clue.text: Italian PM about to take care of country

parts.note: Aldo Moro was an Italian prime minister
C stands for circa, meaning about
c/o, CO, is the abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: An Italian premier is about to look after a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is a country in north-west Africa.

clue.text: Our Ted's terribly disturbed

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters are badly scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A friend called Ted is greatly upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Rousted means roused or harassed, so moved on and disturbed.

clue.text: University lad hugging female may be hungry?

indicators.note: the lad hugs the female letter, enclosing it

parts.note: Ned is a lad's name

explanation.surface: A college boy with his arm round a girl may be peckish.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfed means not given food, and so likely to be hungry.

clue.text: See fit European being given a hearing

indicators.note: a hearing is listening, so these words say the word for a European is heard spoken

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark

explanation.surface: A European decides it is appropriate to let someone speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to see fit, condescending to do something.

clue.text: Order an assortment over the phone

indicators.note: on the telephone you only hear words, so this signals the sound of the phrase

parts.note: a range is an assortment

explanation.surface: Ordering a selection of goods by telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things is to put them in order.

clue.text: After a makeover, I enter fit for a queen

indicators.note: a makeover remodels something, so the letters of I enter fit are remade

explanation.surface: Someone claims a makeover has made them look fit for royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was an Egyptian queen, wife of the pharaoh Akhenaten.

clue.text: Small farm vehicle that's emptied out frequently

indicators.note: emptying removes the inside, so the vehicle loses its middle letter

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
oft is an old word for frequently, as in oft-repeated

explanation.surface: A farm vehicle is emptied often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's emptied' takes the middle letter out of CAR, leaving CR.
explanation.definitionFit: A croft is a small rented farm, especially in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Routinely alternating times at home and times travelling?

parts.note: a day in is time spent at home
a day out is time spent on an outing

explanation.surface: Life swings between staying home and going on trips.
explanation.definitionFit: Day in, day out means every day without variation, so routinely.
